column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4: sizes the world-priced part of the index (39.2%; metal 23.3% about equal to wages 23.8%); Keel's grouping of DGBAS 2021 weights, whose materials, services and wages tie to Q10c-001; reproduces.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 7: corrects SKELETON 3e's led lately by wages (card Q10c): of October's +7.18% (NUMBERS 8d, 120.50) materials gave 4.99 points, wages 1.90; every contribution reproduces from the data file.
Wed 18 Nov: store: electrical +17.44% and its 2.28 points reproduce; extends Q10c-007 (September) to October; a small residency's electrical share is unknown.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 7: reconciles Q10c-010 with the year (wage-led only since May, materials-led over the year); +5.24% and +1.46% match NUMBERS 8d; contributions reproduce.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e wording: wage-led in the press meant fastest-growing, so say wages rising fastest and materials adding most; Aug and Sep figures reproduce and tie to Q10-019 and Q10c-010.
Wed 18 Nov: 3b and 3e: the year's +7.18% was +1.64% in US dollars as the NT$ weakened 5.16% (monthly averages, not NUMBERS 8d's 32.768 of 6 Nov); reproduces; a one-year snapshot, never a trend.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e: the statistical base of row 14, a stronger NT$ came with a rising index at 12 months; every r and slope reproduces; correlation, not cause.
Wed 18 Nov: store: answers the claim's within months with 6-month windows; reproduces; supports row 7 and does no part's job alone.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 7: splits Q10e-011's +0.27 into its parts, a metals story; reproduces; the basis of row 41's watch.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the building sub-index does not soften the finding (24-month r +0.35, median +8.2%); reproduces; covers new building, not conversion.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e: the honest size of the imagined offset, about -0.1% per 1% stronger NT$ holding world prices; reproduces; always add not distinguishable from zero, and carry row 12's 0.5% and 9.4% sizes here (script section 8 uses this regression).
Wed 18 Nov: robustness check of row 11 by distributed lag; cumulative -0.10 and -0.12 reproduce; its sizes come from row 11's regression.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e: why the claim fails, a weaker US dollar came with dearer world goods (+0.47 base metals, +0.57 all imports); reproduces; pair with row 31's warning.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b and 3e: the core find: in the 30 two-year spans with the NT$ 10% or more stronger, materials rose a median 9.9% (3.5% otherwise), metal 27.0%; every figure reproduces; seven episodes, overlapping windows.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b, 3e and Table 3 row 7 aha: a 10% stronger NT$ arrived as a median 22.3% dearer NT$ building in US dollars, never under 9.3%, beating the currency in 25 of 30; reproduces; say about twice the 10% trigger, about 1.6 times the move itself.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e: the two named risks add, the currency a median 65% of the US$ rise in logs (39% to 118%); reproduces; one clause beside row 15 at most.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e's limit and aha row 9: the parts behind Q85-026's +28.0% and Q10e-013's 2002-04 (metal +30.6%, wages +2.8%, US$ base metals +58.1%); reproduces; NCCU's 2004 figures from source.
Wed 18 Nov: store: figures reproduce, but the NT$'s largest two-year rise must say since 1991: NUMBERS 8j's real-currency record has 1986-88 at +29.4%.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the 2016-18 steel-led case (US$ iron and steel +36.1%, rebar +50.5%); reproduces; adds the parts to Q10e-013's 2016-18 +19.5%.
Wed 18 Nov: store: adds the parts to Q10e-007's Aug 2019 to Aug 2021 +29.0% (metal +30.2%, wages +10.5%); reproduces; the shape nearest 2026.

Wed 18 Nov: store or a 3e clause: even when the mechanism showed (1998-2000) the offset was under 1% of the budget; reproduces; 1998 has two clusters of windows, so say the one period, not the one episode.
Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 7: the 2024-25 case, falling world steel let materials dip with a stronger NT$ and it reversed within a year; reproduces; the watch's falling-together case.
Wed 18 Nov: 3b on Laura's calendar: 9 January-to-January windows with the NT$ 5% or more stronger, materials up in 8, US$ cost beat the move in 8; reproduces; 2003's +28.0% equals Q85-026.

Wed 18 Nov: store: 49 windows and +5.2% reproduce only with NT$ per US$ up 10% or more; on the card's own convention (10% fewer US$) it is 38 windows and +5.7%; name the convention and add the line to the script.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4: the 10.1% fall (84.19 to 75.66), the May 2012 regain and services -6.95% reproduce, but below its year-earlier level every month Apr 1996 to Jan 2004 is false (Apr to Dec 1998 were not); say Apr 1996 to Mar 1998 and Jan 1999 to Jan 2004; fix the card's Part 4 too.

Wed 18 Nov: store, beside row 25: NCCU names the slump and migrant labour; +17.0% is the wage index's 1991-93 annual-average rise and -0.20% a year sits by the data's 1994-2007 -0.22%; a yearbook's stated cause, not tested.

Wed 18 Nov: store: labour-supply policy moves Taiwan's construction wages; counts from secondary tables of Ministry data, one article read as abstract; the 2031-33 quota effect is a reading, not a forecast.

Wed 18 Nov: store: the link is weaker, not gone: the -0.09 since 2006 is same-window while the +0.30 is lagged six months over the whole span; lagged six months since 2006 r is +0.24 (Keel check), so never has gone.
Wed 18 Nov: store or a 3e clause: materials do fall fast, in world slumps (-21.72% to Jun 2009, metal -44.04%, with the NT$ 7.3% weaker); reproduces; partly Q103-014 and Q10c-003's 2009 fall.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 4: the two risks are about equal in size over two years (sd 0.074 currency, 0.072 index) and add; reproduces; supports NUMBERS 8q's one series.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e honesty: BIS says the dollar-commodity link broke in 2021-22 and may weaken, so row 15's pattern is a record, not a law; read at source in part.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the ECB's oil-dollar link since the early 2000s matches Taiwan's era split (+0.17, +0.36 reproduce); oil is under 2% of the index.
Wed 18 Nov: store: at the border the currency passes through whole (May 2025 -2.60% in US$, -9.05% in NT$; 81.3% invoiced in US$); read at source in part; about imports, not construction.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: abstract read, full text not; import prices, not construction.
Wed 18 Nov: store and Table 3 row 7's watch: Feng Hsin's weekly rebar quote is an early read before DGBAS's month; a company call and trade notes, read in part.
Wed 18 Nov: store: DGBAS's pricing days show no measurement lag hides a steel fall; the 2021 base is assumed to price as the 2016 base did.
Wed 18 Nov: store or a 3e clause: Taiwan's own rules moved costs fastest (1992 +21.77%, sand +76.7% as an annual average, 2006 +22.84%); reproduces; extends Q10e-014.
Wed 18 Nov: store, prior art: development-bank contracts split a price by currency of payment, so to Laura the whole NT$ budget is the foreign part; the facility contract is out of scope.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the template's local labour (6-10%) is far below DGBAS's wages (23.8%), so the same rough split as DGBAS's weights is false; keep only the conversion into the payment currency.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b: the $25,600 and $33,400 needs are Keel arithmetic, not in NUMBERS; register them in 8q or say the median strong-NT$ rise sits inside 8q's central 24.9%; $28,682, 24.9% and $3,509 check against NUMBERS 4 and 8q.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 7: fix about twice the currency move: the median US$ rise is 2.2 times the 10% trigger but 1.6 times the actual move (median 11.7%, Keel check); a watch, never a rule; the pair's size stays out of the table (SKELETON).
Wed 18 Nov: 3e wording guard: right to bar any offset, but name the condition (two-year spans with the NT$ 10% or more stronger) for the 9.9%, and add not distinguishable from zero to the 0.5%.
